answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that deposit if later evidence proves coordinated fraud. Splitting one stake across a hundred aliases does not create a hundred times the influence: each identity must immobilize its own capital, and fake accounts risk losing it. A beacon can publish the lock and slashing rules; jade and lagoon might simply label two test agents, not confer extra trust. The attacker pays in capital and time, while honest newcomers face the same entry cost.
